title: Providing Safe Space for Honest Mistakes in the Public Sector Is the Most Important Predictor for Work Engagement after Strategic Clarity
short_title: Safe Space for Honest Mistakes and Public Sector Work Engagement

affiliations.1: Department of Psychology, Reichman University, Herzliya 4610101, Israel; thais.gargantinicard@post.idc.ac.il
affiliations.2: Center for Advanced Hindsight, Duke University, Durham, NC 27708, USA; michael.daly@duke.edu (M.D.); jjs92@duke.edu (J.S.)

abstract: Multiple studies highlight the link between engagement at work and performance, influencing organizations to put more effort into improving employee engagement levels. In this study, we begin to examine the influence of multiple psychological parameters on employees’ work engagement (WE) within the public sector. The idea is to break the concept of WE down into eight individually measurable parameters that will allow for a better understanding and development of stronger interventions. Based on this analysis, we reproduce the outcome that strategic clarity is the most connected property to WE. More importantly, we introduce a new concept, honest mistakes, and show that having a safe space for making mistakes and learning from it is the second most important property of WE. This result is of interest, as allowing mistakes, even if they were made innocently, is considered taboo in the public sector. These outcomes are based on the reports of n=7682 public sector employees from Brazil. In particular, the analysis shows that these outcomes hold for both professional and management positions across the health, administrative, justice, police, social work, and education offices.
summary: Engagement at work is linked to performance, so we examined which psychological factors drive work engagement among public sector employees, breaking it into eight measurable parameters. Using reports from 7682 public sector employees in Brazil, we confirmed that strategic clarity is most connected to engagement, and found that having a safe space to make honest mistakes and learn from them is the second most important factor. This held for both professional and management positions across several types of government offices.
key_findings: Strategic clarity is the property most connected to work engagement, reproducing earlier outcomes.
Having a safe space to make honest mistakes and learn from them is the second most important property of work engagement.
This matters because allowing mistakes, even innocent ones, is considered taboo in the public sector.
Results hold for professional and management positions across health, administrative, justice, police, social work and education offices.
